newsitem.title: USA: Juror screening under way in Florida tobacco trial.
newsitem.headline: Juror screening under way in Florida tobacco trial.

text.p: A Florida judge began screening candidates Monday to serve on the jury that will hear Florida's landmark $1 billion lawsuit against the tobacco industry.

The state is seeking to recover money spent to treat sick smokers and has accused the major cigarette makers of racketeering, an allegation that could force the industry to hand over billions of dollars in past profits.
The Florida lawsuit is the first of 40 filed by U.S. state attorneys general to reach trial and is being watched closely by legal scholars and tobacco stock analysts.
Palm Beach Circuit Judge Harold Cohen gave initial approval to 12 of the first 28 candidates from a jury pool of more than 300. Of the 12, seven had never smoked, three had quit and two were smokers.
The prospective jurors were to be questioned further on August 18 when lawyers for Florida and the tobacco companies will begin final selection of six jurors and nine alternates.
